## Preliminary Analysis of Household Food Security in British Columbia, 2024

# Question

What is the estimated number of people in British Columbia by household food security status in 2024?

# Setup + summary

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

foodinsecurity <- read_csv("data/13100835.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

summary(foodinsecurity)
```

# Cohort 

We restricted the prepared file to records for British Columbia only. Missing values were counted before complete-case rows were selected for the grouped results.
```{r}
BC_cohort <- foodinsecurity |>
  filter(GEO=='British Columbia')

cohort_counts <- tibble(
  step = c("Prepared file", "After British Columbia restriction"),
  n = c(nrow(foodinsecurity), nrow(BC_cohort))
)

kable(cohort_counts)
```


# Missingness Table

```{r}
key_vars <- c("GEO", "Demographic characteristics", "Household food security status", "REF_DATE", "VALUE")

missingness <- tibble(variable = key_vars) |>
  mutate(
    missing_n = vapply(
      BC_cohort[key_vars],
      function(x) sum(is.na(x)),
      numeric(1)
    ),
    missing_percent = round(100 * missing_n / nrow(BC_cohort), 1)
  )

write_csv(
  missingness,
  "milestones/m2-preliminary-analysis/submission/missingness-summary.csv"
)

kable(missingness)
```

# Table 1-style summary

```{r}
latest_year <- BC_cohort |>
  filter(
    `Demographic characteristics` == "All persons",
    Statistics == "Number of persons"
  ) |>
  summarise(year = max(as.integer(REF_DATE), na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(year)

table1 <- BC_cohort |>
  filter(
    `Demographic characteristics` == "All persons",
    Statistics == "Number of persons",
    as.integer(REF_DATE) == latest_year,
    `Household food security status` %in% c(
      "Food secure",
      "Food insecure, marginal",
      "Food insecure, moderate",
      "Food insecure, severe"
    )
  ) |>
  transmute(
    `Food security status` = `Household food security status`,
    `Estimated people` = VALUE
  )

knitr::kable(table1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

# Preliminary Analysis Figure

```{r}
ggplot(
  table1,
  aes(
    x = reorder(`Food security status`, `Estimated people`),
    y = `Estimated people`,
    fill = `Food security status`
  )
) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = scales::comma(`Estimated people`)),
    hjust = -0.15
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = paste(
      "Estimated number of people by household food\n security status, British Columbia,",
      latest_year
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = "Estimated persons",
    caption = paste(
      "Estimated number of persons by household food security status in\n British Columbia, 2024. Values are weighted estimates and descriptive.\n Source: Statistics Canada, Table 13-10-0835-01."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


# Interpretation

In 2024, most people in British Columbia were estimated to be food secure (4,254,000). Among the plotted food-insecure categories, moderate food insecurity had the largest estimate (644,800), compared with marginal (317,500) and severe (319,300).

# What this analysis cannot claim

The figures are population estimates, not individual headcounts. This chart cannot explain causes, compare demographic subgroups, establish trends, or show that one factor caused another.
